source_passages.quotation: - **Craft:** Exhaust one hammer per crafting icon; pawn acts as crafting piece matching current clearing, and may activate repeatedly despite normal once-per-turn crafting limit. Clearing must match **all icons**; cannot craft mixed fox/rabbit/mouse requirements from one clearing. When you craft an item, you may immediately take that item face up into Satchel/track and **use it for another Daylight action immediately**, if its cost and other requirements are met. Need supply item as usual.

answer.ruling: No. The pawn’s current clearing must match all icons, so one clearing cannot pay mixed fox/rabbit/mouse requirements.
The pawn may activate repeatedly despite the normal once-per-turn crafting-piece limit, but each icon still costs one exhausted hammer.

When crafting an item, the Vagabond may immediately take it face up into Satchel or a track and use it for another Daylight action immediately, if its cost and other requirements are met; the item must be available in supply.

source_passages.quotation:
| Base character | Starting items | Special action |
|---|---|---|
| Thief | boot, torch, tea, sword | **Steal:** exhaust torch to take random hand card from player with faction pieces in your clearing |
| Tinker | boot, torch, bag, hammer | **Day Labor:** exhaust torch to take discard-pile card matching clearing; bird always qualifies |
| Ranger | boot, torch, crossbow, sword | **Hideout:** exhaust torch to repair three items, keeping their faces; immediately end Daylight and begin Evening |

answer.part: base characters, starting items, special action costs and results
answer.ruling: Thief starts with boot, torch, tea, sword; Steal exhausts torch to take a random hand card from a player with faction pieces in the Vagabond’s clearing. Tinker starts with boot, torch, bag, hammer; Day Labor exhausts torch to take a discard-pile card matching the clearing (a bird always qualifies). Ranger starts with boot, torch, crossbow, sword; Hideout exhausts torch to repair three items while keeping their faces, then immediately ends Daylight and begins Evening.

source_passages.quotation: Clearings have fox, rabbit or mouse suit and limited building slots. Buildings require open slots; tokens do not occupy these. Ruins block their slots and can be removed only when explicitly allowed. A forest is enclosed by printed paths and clearings; it is adjacent to clearings touching it without crossing a printed path and to forests separated by just one printed path. Winter's river also divides forests. (2.2–2.4, M.1–2.)
- **Explore:** Exhaust torch in ruin's clearing. Take one hidden item face up into Satchel or track; score one VP if an item taken. Remove ruin when its last item is taken, freeing the building slot.

answer.part: removing last item and building slot
answer.ruling: Ruins block building slots and may be removed only when explicitly allowed. Exploring exhausts a torch in the ruin’s clearing; when the last hidden item is taken, remove the ruin and free the building slot.
Ordinary building placement cannot remove a ruin; removal requires an explicit rule allowing it.

source_passages.quotation: **Vagabond coalition (9.2.8):** Cannot activate normal dominance win. With **four or more players**, during own Daylight at **at least 10 VP**, activate dominance to coalition with another player **not already in coalition**, whose VP is lowest among players other than you (choose among ties). Put your score marker on partner's faction board and stop scoring. If partner wins, you also win, including if partner wins through dominance. Coalition partners are not enemies. A Hostile partner becomes Indifferent. Coalition does not by itself grant Allied relationship powers.

answer.part: coalition partner as enemy and Allied benefits
answer.ruling: Coalition partners are not enemies, so a coalition partner cannot be chosen as an enemy to attack. Coalition does not itself grant Allied relationship powers.

source_passages.quotation:
- **Hostile:** Removing **one** warrior of a non-Hostile faction immediately moves marker to Hostile (except allied battle-loss rule above). **Infamy:** During battle on your own turn, score **one extra VP per hostile piece removed**, except warrior that first made faction Hostile. **Each hostile building/token removed in battle on your turn normally scores two VP: one removal VP plus one Infamy. A hostile warrior scores one Infamy, except the warrior that first caused Hostile status.** Infamy depends on whose turn it is, rather than which side attacks: no Infamy on another player's turn, and none from Strike. Hostile status requires extra boot for moves into hostile warriors, not merely buildings/tokens.
- Aid cannot move marker out of Hostile; it can still obtain a crafted item. Coalition with Hostile faction resets its marker to Indifferent.

**Ordinary removal VP (3.2.1):**

| Removed enemy piece | Ordinary removal VP |
|---|---|
| Warrior | **0 VP** |
| Building | **1 VP** |
| Token | **1 VP** |

Faction/card scoring can add to these ordinary points. In particular, Vagabond Infamy is an **additional** point per eligible Hostile piece in battle on his own turn, except the warrior that first caused Hostile status. Do not add an ordinary removal point for a warrior.

answer.ruling: Total: 3 VP. The first warrior removed immediately makes the previously non-Hostile faction Hostile, but that warrior earns no Infamy and warriors earn no ordinary removal VP (0 VP). The second warrior is hostile and earns 1 Infamy VP. Removing the hostile building in battle on the Vagabond’s own turn earns 1 ordinary removal VP plus 1 Infamy VP, for 2 VP. Sum: 0 + 1 + 2 = 3 VP.

source_passages.quotation: - **Move:** Exhaust one boot, plus **one extra boot** if destination has any warriors of any Hostile faction (also for forced moves). Ignore rule. **Cannot enter a forest with this action; from a forest you may move only to an adjacent clearing.** Slip has the special free-boot exception.

- **Hostile:** Removing **one** warrior of a non-Hostile faction immediately moves marker to Hostile (except allied battle-loss rule above). **Infamy:** During battle on your own turn, score **one extra VP per hostile piece removed**, except warrior that first made faction Hostile. **Each hostile building/token removed in battle on your turn normally scores two VP: one removal VP plus one Infamy. A hostile warrior scores one Infamy, except the warrior that first caused Hostile status.** Infamy depends on whose turn it is, rather than which side attacks: no Infamy on another player's turn, and none from Strike. Hostile status requires extra boot for moves into hostile warriors, not merely buildings/tokens.

answer.part: normal Move cost in hostile-building-only clearing
answer.ruling: Exhaust one boot. Hostile buildings alone do not trigger the extra boot; the extra cost applies when the destination has hostile warriors.

answer.part: normal Move cost with hostile warriors from multiple factions
answer.ruling: Exhaust one boot plus one extra boot if the destination contains any warriors of any Hostile faction. Multiple hostile factions do not add further boots.

source_passages.quotation: **Dominance (3.3):** In own Daylight at **at least 10 VP**, activate a dominance card from hand into play area; remove score marker and stop scoring VP. Cannot remove/replace activated card. At **start of own Birdsong**, win if ruling **three clearings of matching mouse/rabbit/fox suit**, or for **bird dominance, two diagonally opposite corner clearings**. Meeting condition earlier does not immediately win. Dominance cards cannot be crafted, but can be spent for suit. Whenever one would enter discard, put it near map available instead. During own Daylight, spend matching card to take available dominance into hand. Available **bird dominance remains bird**, so payment must be bird; a bird hand card can pay for non-bird dominance. Activation and taking are separate, neither requires a faction action allowance.

answer.part: taking card does not activate dominance and action allowance
answer.ruling: No. During own Daylight, spending a matching card to take an available dominance card puts it in hand; it does not activate it. Taking and activating are separate, and neither uses a faction action allowance, including for the Marquise. Activation itself requires own Daylight at 10 or more VP.

source_passages.quotation: The base game has a Fall/Winter board, two battle dice, four faction boards, 54 shared-deck cards, 16 faction overviews, 4 Eyrie leaders and 2 Loyal Viziers, 3 Vagabond characters and 15 quests. There are 25 Marquise, 20 Eyrie and 10 Alliance warriors; one Vagabond pawn; 7 roosts, 6 each of sawmills, workshops and recruiters, 3 bases; 10 sympathy, 8 wood and 1 keep token; 4 ruins, 4 score markers, 3 relationship markers, 12 clearing markers and 23 items. Items are boots, swords, bags, hammers, tea, coins, crossbows and a torch. Items are not faction pieces or enemy pieces. **Faction-piece ownership cannot change**: each player owns the faction chosen in setup and its listed faction pieces, except items; possessing an item does not make it faction-owned.

answer.part: ownership of faction pieces and items
answer.ruling: Ownership of faction pieces cannot change. Each player owns the faction chosen in setup and its listed faction pieces, except items. Items are not faction pieces or enemy pieces, and possessing an item does not make it faction-owned.

source_passages.section: Crafting — component destinations and card treatment
source_passages.quotation:
| Separate component after a successful craft | Starts in | Goes to |
|---|---|---|
| Immediate-effect crafting card | Your hand | Shared discard pile after resolving |
| Persistent-effect crafting card | Your hand | Your play area |
| Item token produced by an item card | Map item supply | Crafting faction’s Crafted Items box; when Vagabond itself crafts, it may immediately take its crafted item face up into Satchel/track |

- Persistent effect (stone box): keep card in your play area and gain its text, subject to the personal duplicate check above. Its card is outside your hand and cannot be spent/discarded/used for another purpose unless explicitly instructed.
- **Ambush cards cannot be crafted:** the defender may play one for two immediate hits, or the attacker may play one to foil a defending ambush, matching the clearing. **Dominance cards cannot be crafted:** activate one to change victory condition, or spend it for suit.

answer.ruling: After an immediate effect resolves, discard its crafting card from hand to the shared discard pile. Keep a persistent-effect crafting card from hand in your play area. An item token made by a craft comes from map supply into the crafting faction’s Crafted Items box (with the Vagabond’s stated option to take its own item into Satchel/track).

answer.ruling: A persistent card in your play area is outside your hand and cannot be spent, discarded, or used for another purpose unless explicitly instructed.

source_passages.quotation: - **Ambush cards cannot be crafted:** the defender may play one for two immediate hits, or the attacker may play one to foil a defending ambush, matching the clearing. **Dominance cards cannot be crafted:** activate one to change victory condition, or spend it for suit.

answer.part: whether Ambush and dominance cards can be crafted and permitted uses
answer.ruling: Neither Ambush nor dominance cards can be crafted. A defender may play a matching Ambush for two immediate hits; an attacker may play a matching Ambush to foil a defending Ambush. A dominance card may be activated to change the victory condition or spent for suit.

source_passages.quotation: **30 VP:** First to 30 wins immediately, on any player's turn. If multiple reach 30 simultaneously, tied player closest clockwise to current player wins, including current player. Removing enemy buildings/tokens gives one VP each regardless of phase or whether attacker/defender. Crafting items scores printed VP except Eyrie's Disdain. Faction scoring is described above. (3.1–2.)

answer.ruling: The first player to reach 30 VP wins immediately on any player’s turn; they do not finish the action, phase, or turn first.

source_passages.quotation: **Battle (4.3):** Choose a clearing with your warriors or pawn and an enemy there as defender. **Battle does not require you to rule the clearing.** Resolve these six steps:

answer.ruling: To initiate battle, choose a clearing containing your warriors or pawn and an enemy there as defender. You do not need to rule that clearing.

source_passages.quotation:
2. **Before-roll effects:** Resolve applicable effects; attacker chooses order if both have them.
3. **Roll:** Higher die is attacker's rolled hits, lower defender's; equal dice give equal results. Each side's rolled hits are capped by its own warriors in battle. Alliance defending reverses the dice; Vagabond uses undamaged swords instead of warriors.
4. **After-roll effects:** Resolve effects affecting battle that do not say “before rolling”; attacker chooses order if both have them.

6. **Deal hits:** Each hit removes one opposing piece. The side taking hits chooses its own removal order, but **all its warriors must be removed before its buildings/tokens**. It also chooses order of effects triggered by its pieces' removal. Both sides deal their counted hits; losing warriors does not retroactively change the rolled cap. Whoever removes an enemy building/token scores **one VP each**, even while defending and even outside battle. Vagabond takes hits as item damage instead.

answer.ruling: Resolve applicable before-roll effects; if both sides have such effects, the attacker chooses their order. Resolve after-roll effects that do not say before rolling; if both have them, the attacker chooses their order.
The side taking hits chooses the order of effects triggered by its pieces’ removal.

source_passages.quotation: 5. **Count hits:** Add extra hits (uncapped by warriors), subtract ignored hits. If defender has no warriors, attacker deals one extra hit for **defenseless**; Vagabond is instead defenseless if it has no undamaged swords.

answer.ruling: In Count Hits, add extra hits (which are uncapped by warriors) and subtract ignored hits from the hit total. If the defender has no warriors, the attacker adds one defenseless hit; for Vagabond, defenseless means no undamaged swords.
